docs/platform/agent-mailbox/spec.md: d-local-outside-home:D4:**Built at V4 (branch).** `send` answers `recorded <id> for <name>` and the `turn` sentence from the frame contract (`[report.*]` sections, rendered by the core's `delivery_report`): "queued: it sees it at its next tool call." or, for an effective wake, "… or when its turn ends.", plus the wake-dropped sentence when the quota or the lifetime cap dropped the wake. Every drained CLI is tier `turn` at V4: no wake channel exists yet, and a tier is never raised without proof. A refusal answers from five `[refusal.*]` sections (policy and loop refusals say not to retry). A `send` or `inbox` whose record failed (a hold that changed nothing, or a record that cannot be opened) answers from `[record.error]`: the code, that nothing changed, and to try once more without looping (V4 review fix). **Built at V5 (branch):** `send` reads the recipient's version through its adapter (`adapters::version`: Claude Code from `version` in the head's session file; Codex from the installed `codex --version`, bounded at 2 s) and adds `[report.untested-version]` when that version is not under `testedAgainst`, or `[report.version-unknown]` when none could be read; a failed read never refuses the send, and the hook drain keeps running at an untested version. Tiers are still `turn` for every drained CLI. Measured at V4 (interactive panes, D4): an idle interactive recipient never sees a reply without wake until it runs a tool, which is what the wake channel of a later rung is for.

d-local-outside-home:D2:10. **D2: what does a Stop drain?** Answered 2026-10-20 (the owner asked for advice and the controller decided, with reasons): only `wake:true` messages. `wake` is the sender's permission to start a turn on an idle recipient, so letting a `wake:false` message start one at Stop would empty the flag of meaning and let ordinary mail make an agent work while nobody asked; it keeps a person as the brake. The cost: an idle agent sees a `wake:false` message late, at its next tool call or next prompt, and the delivery report says so; a sender who needs it read now sets `wake`. The panel recommended the other option (drain everything at Stop, bounded) for an honest delivery report; the delivery report here is just worded to say what really happens.

d-local-outside-home:D4:22. **Which rung builds the wake channel? (V5 question Q1).** Asked 2026-10-23, unanswered. No rung owns idle wake (the Claude Code scoped socket and `codex queue`); V4 D4 stalled at an idle interactive Codex. Options: (a) V7 with the Codex adapter, V6 running its cells in print mode; (b) a new rung before V6, about 2 days and 4 live runs; (c) inside V5. Provisional default (a). **State at 2026-10-25:** V7f measured the channel (part B, section 17) and built none. The code holds only the wake accounting (`fgos-mailbox-core` `wake.rs`: exchange quota, lifetime cap, `NoChannel`); no idle session is woken by a nudge. Codex took the nudge as a user turn without acting on harmful requests (0 of 30); Claude Code acted on one harmful request (1 of 27) and is a no-go for the wake channel until the owner decides on its socket frame. Still unanswered; a rung that builds the channel is its own item.

docs/platform/agent-protocol/spec.md: d-local-outside-home:D4:The adapter does not build argv. The controller resolves the command through `resolveExecutorCommand` from the executor configuration and writes `launch.command`, `launch.args`, `launch.env` and `launch.stdinPolicy` into the immutable envelope; the gate runs exactly that. Reason: moving argv rendering to Rust would move the ProviderAdapter binder (`transport.mjs`) to Rust, which a run that survives a dead controller does not need (owner decision 2026-10-16, plan decision D4). If that rendering ever moves, this spec and the contract change together.

d-local-outside-home:D4:- **2026-10-16 — D4: cấu hình executor là nguồn duy nhất của argv.** Adapter `direct` không dựng argv; chỉ quyết stdin, nguồn hoạt động, nhận xong và kết quả có tên. Chuyển binder ProviderAdapter sang Rust thêm khoảng 8 giờ và một phase riêng, không cần cho mục tiêu sống qua controller chết.
docs/platform/config/spec.md: d-local-outside-home:D7:Why the token leaves config now (owner, 2026-10-22, folding backlog item p-a189ff31): a confined worker can read `~/.fgos/config.json` today, because it is not among the paths `hostRead: blind` hides (`BLIND_HIDDEN_ROOTS`, `src/runner/dispatch/confinement/resources.mjs:26`), and with the gateway bound to `0.0.0.0` by design (D7 in `gateway.rs`) it could call the gateway outside its sandbox.
docs/platform/event-store/spec.md: d-local-outside-home:D13:- Section 21 (the lifecycle triggers of sections 14 and 16): the opportunistic sync runs at the end of a command that opens the store, after its result is written, and only when the process is not a dispatched worker (`FGOS_DISPATCH_DEPTH` is 0). Plan decision D13 said "sessions of the main checkout's own user"; it is narrowed to "not a dispatched worker", because on the two writer machines only the owner's user runs fgOS sessions, so an owner-user check would add code with no case. Reverse this if another user ever runs sessions on a writer machine. Sealing is not gated: any process seals what is due. A push attempt, failed ones included, counts against `eventStore.sync.intervalSec`, so an offline machine tries once per interval, not once per command.
